note: Changga survive mostly as songs, not period records: every track here is a later recording (1977-2019) of a changga, by trot-era singers on nostalgia anthologies (Shin Canarya and Hwang Geum Sim began in the 1930s), and of patriotic songs on a 1988 independence-song album. Three songs carry most of the list: the school song 학도가, the 1920s favourite 희망가 and the 1926 waltz 사의 찬미, the first yuhaeng changga.

size.basis: No source counts recordings; this is a judgement. Changga were mostly sung in schools, churches, rallies and from songbooks, not recorded: the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture names songbooks (Lee Sang-jun's Middle School Songbook and Newest Songbook; three 1920s yuhaeng changga songbooks of 1922 and 1927) and says independence-army songs were most numerous around 1910-1920, but commercial records only began in the 1920s (학도가 first recorded in 1921, 사의 찬미 in 1926). What can be heard today is a few dozen period 78s and many later re-recordings of a small repertoire (학도가, 희망가, 사의 찬미, 독립군가 and other patriotic songs) on trot-era nostalgia anthologies and independence-song albums. An insider's essential list is about 15 songs, most of them the same titles in different voices.
